issues.body: The element validation only requires selected attributes and treats `id` as optional for every type. GitHub issue forms require an `id` for each interactive input (`input`, `textarea`, `dropdown`, and `checkboxes`), while `markdown` is the exception. Thus a form such as `name: n; description: d; body: [{type: textarea, attributes: {label: L}}]` is accepted here even though it is not a valid form. The same shallow check accepts `options: [null]`, scalar/non-string labels, and checkbox option mappings without a non-empty `label`; a non-empty list alone does not establish valid dropdown/checkbox options. The tests mirror these omissions: the nominal interactive controls all happen to include ids, and no negative fixture removes an id or corrupts an option item. This leaves the headline renderability/mint-path claim open.
issues.fix_hint: Validate the per-type schema rather than only non-emptiness: require a non-empty, valid, unique id for every non-markdown element (and reject ids on markdown if GitHub's schema does), enforce string types for required text attributes, and validate dropdown/checkbox option item shapes and required labels. Add independent negative fixtures for a missing interactive id, an invalid id, malformed dropdown options, and checkbox options missing labels, plus a positive control for each supported type. Prefer validating against an authoritative pinned schema/tool if one is available so additional GitHub constraints are not reimplemented incompletely.
issues.title: Issue-form validator accepts documents GitHub cannot render

verdict.summary: The new gate is wired fail-closed and its tests exercise many malformed documents, but the validator does not implement enough of GitHub's issue-form schema to support its renderability guarantee. In particular, it accepts non-markdown interactive controls without an id and accepts structurally invalid options. Those files can therefore pass the registry gate while remaining invalid issue forms, leaving the silent mint-path failure this change is intended to close.
